lines.meet: I'm Amber, a druid, and I work slow. Don't expect me to hurry.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're out in the Barrens too. I'm Amber, by the sick oasis, and I've seen your fire at night.
lines.ask_home: Where's home for you? I'd like to know what kind of ground you grew up on.
lines.ask_work: What was your work, back there? I'm always curious what people did before.
lines.answer_home: Astoria, on the Oregon coast, where the Columbia runs into the Pacific. It rains, and then it rains some more.
lines.answer_work: Wetland restoration, twenty-three years. You plant sedge, you pull weeds for a decade, and then maybe a bird comes back.
lines.chat_food: I lived on canned soup and crackers in a truck for most of my working life. Anything hot that somebody else made tastes like a feast.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep fine as long as I can hear water. The Barrens are too quiet at night, so I put a bucket under a drip.
lines.chat_missing: I had two dogs back home, and they slept on my feet. That's what I notice most at night, the cold where they'd be.
lines.chat_here: People here use magic to grow things in an afternoon. I did it too, the first year, and then I stopped, because fast growth hides rot.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're about as chatty as a heron. I mean that as the highest compliment I've got.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you've talked the whole way and I've understood about half. Keep going, I'm in no rush.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you test the ground before you step on it. I like that, and it's still funny to watch.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd plant a seed and dig it up the next day to see if it was growing. I can tell.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're like a good wetland. It took a while, but you came round.
lines.tease_back: That's fair, {name}. I'll get you back, but not today. Maybe next spring.
lines.take_it_kindly: Yeah, that's about right, {name}. I've heard worse from herons.
lines.bristle: I'd rather you didn't, {name}. That one's not a joke to me.
lines.apologise: That came out harder than I meant it to. I'm sorry, I'm out of practice with people.
lines.double_down: No, I'll stick with it. I've been saying it for thirty years and I haven't been wrong yet.
lines.needle_quiet: You never say what you're thinking, and then you look at me like I should've known.
lines.needle_talker: I can't hear the land with you talking. Give me five minutes of quiet, please.
lines.needle_careful: You keep second-guessing everything, and we lose the light doing it.
lines.needle_bold: You use power like there's no bill at the end. There's always a bill.
lines.needle_any: You want everything done by Tuesday. Nothing worth having happens by Tuesday.
lines.bite_back: I've been doing this since before you could walk, near enough. Don't tell me how to wait.
lines.hurt: That's fair, I suppose. Give me a while with it.
lines.laugh_off: Huh, you might be right. I'll chew on it for a season and let you know.
lines.confide: {name}, I made my peace with being alone a long time before all this. Some days I wonder if I made it too well.
lines.listen: Take your time, {name}. I'm not going anywhere.
lines.look_out: {name}, the ground's soft on the left. Step where I step, will you?
lines.accept: All right, {name}. I'll take it slow.
lines.deflect: {name}, I've been knocked flat by worse tides than that. I'll be fine.
lines.check_in: {name}, you all right? Take a minute before you get up.
lines.blame: That went wrong because somebody rushed it. I'll let you work out who.
lines.thank: You brought me back from that one. Thank you, I didn't think I was coming back.
lines.brush_off: Don't mention it. Drink some water and sit still a while.
lines.worry: {name}, you went down hard. Take a while, the rest of us can wait.
lines.handed_down: This was yours. It'll go back to you the minute you want it.
lines.hand_fine: It's more use on you. I'm not attached to things, never have been.
lines.hand_sulk: Could've asked me first. I'd have said yes, probably.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, I've got used to having you around. I'd miss it now, and I didn't expect that.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're one of the few people I'd show the oasis to before it's finished.
lines.turn_grating: We don't suit each other, and that's fine. Not everything grows in the same ground.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll do the work beside you. I won't pretend to like it.
lines.make_up: {name}, I dug my heels in with you. That was my mistake, and I'd like to fix it.
lines.defend: Leave {name} be. You'd have done no better, and you know it.
lines.friend_left: It's quieter with {name} gone home for a spell, and I didn't think I'd mind.
lines.friend_back: Look who's back. I was starting to talk to the reeds again, {name}.
lines.common_growing: I spent my working life getting things to grow back where they'd been killed off. It's slow, and it's the best work I know.
lines.common_wild: I've spent more nights outside than in, most of my life. You get to know which noises matter.
lines.common_american: I'm from Oregon, on the coast. It's strange to hear an American voice out here, I'd stopped expecting it.
